title: Compte rendu du Conseil des ministres du 10 septembre 2026
key_claim: The French government presented its bill transposing Directive (EU) 2023/970 on 10 September 2026; the current professional-equality index declaration is kept in 2027 and the move to the new index starts from 2028; pay-gap differences above a decree-set threshold of no more than 5% must be justified or corrected; women's average private-sector pay is 21.8% below men's, and the like-for-like gap is 3.6%.
frame_summary: The French government presents a phased transposition that keeps the existing equality index in 2027 so that employers can prepare for the new indicators from 2028.
verbatim_quote: la déclaration actuelle de l’index de l’égalité professionnelle issu de la loi pour la liberté de choisir son avenir professionnel sera maintenue en 2027
verbatim_list: le revenu salarial moyen des femmes reste inférieur de 21,8 % à celui des hommes
d’anticiper le passage au nouvel index à partir de 2028
l’écart de salaire constaté en équivalent temps plein est de 3,6 %
notes: Council of Ministers report in French. Quotes checked by hand against the live page on 07/11/2026 with whitespace normalised.

title: Meer openheid over loonkloof tussen mannen en vrouwen
key_claim: The Dutch government's bill sets the first report, from employers with at least 150 workers, for 7 June 2028 on calendar year 2027 pay differences, assuming entry into force on 1 January 2027; in 2024 women in Dutch business earned on average 14,5% less per hour.
frame_summary: The Dutch government introduces its transposition bill and sets its own reporting calendar, with the first report falling a year after the directive's date.
verbatim_quote: moet dan uiterlijk 7 juni 2028 rapporteren over de loonverschillen in het kalenderjaar 2027
verbatim_list: Het is de bedoeling dat het wetsvoorstel op 1 januari 2027 in werking treedt
In 2024 verdienden vrouwen volgens het CBS in het bedrijfsleven gemiddeld 14,5% minder per uur dan mannen
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band): the government's own statement of the reporting calendar. Page metadata shows DCTERMS.modified 2026-10-01; the dateline is 21-05-2026.

publisher: EUR-Lex (Publications Office of the European Union)
title: Directive (EU) 2023/970 on pay transparency (Article 9, reporting on the pay gap)
date_evidence: Evergreen legal text, accessed 2026-11-07; EUR-Lex metadata eli:date_publication 2023-05-17
key_claim: Article 9 requires employers with 250 or more workers to report by 7 June 2027 and yearly after, and employers with 150 to 249 workers by 7 June 2027 and every three years after, on the previous calendar year.
frame_summary: The directive fixes the first reporting date in the text, addressed to Member States, which must ensure employers report.
verbatim_quote: Employers with 150 to 249 workers shall, by 7 June 2027 and every three years thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.
verbatim_list: Employers with 250 workers or more shall, by 7 June 2027 and every year thereafter, provide the information set out in paragraph 1 relating to the previous calendar year.
notes: Legal act in force, published 17 May 2023; cited as an evergreen reference text, not as a recency source. title: Directive Pay Transparency : la France franchit une nouvelle étape
key_claim: Deloitte's French law practice reports the bill was filed with the Senate on 10 September 2026, that the Assemblée nationale is not expected to examine it before the end of 2026, and that the session should end in February 2027 because of the presidential campaign, making adoption before the election relatively uncertain.
frame_summary: Deloitte's French lawyers argue the calendar for the French bill is tight enough that the delay already accumulated could prove much larger than expected.
verbatim_quote: l’examen du texte par l’Assemblée nationale n’est pas attendu avant la fin de l’année 2026
verbatim_list: la session de l’Assemblée nationale, dont l’ordre du jour est déjà chargé, devrait s’achever en février 2027 en raison de la campagne présidentielle
les chances de voir ce projet adopté avant l’élection présidentielle semblent relativement compromises
notes: French-language Tier 2 source from a major consultancy's law practice.

title: EU Pay Transparency Directive - Implementation Status
key_claim: Lockton's status table as of 23 September 2026 lists Greece, Italy, Lithuania, Malta and Slovakia as fully transposed, Estonia and Poland as partly transposed, and Germany with a draft law prepared but unpublished; Lithuania's reporting duties start 1 January 2027 and most Greek employer duties 1 November 2026.
frame_summary: Lockton presents transposition as uneven, with only a small number of states complete and many still drafting.
verbatim_quote: implementation remains uneven, with only a small number of countries having completed transposition by the deadline and many others still progressing draft legislation
verbatim_list: A draft law has been prepared but has yet to be published.
with pay reporting obligations to take effect from 1 January 2027
However, most employer obligations will only take effect from 1 November 2026
notes: Insurance broker's compliance alert written with a law firm (Claeys & Engels); a compilation of national status. The counts of five fully transposed, two partly transposed, thirteen with a draft only and seven with no published draft are the analyst's own tally of the 27 rows of the table.

title: Wet loontransparantie later dan 1 januari 2027 in werking?
date_evidence: <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-09-21T13:12:46+00:00">; visible: 21 september 2026 door Salaris Vanmorgen
key_claim: Dutch payroll trade press reports the Tweede Kamer plenary debate on the transposition bill is planned for 7 December 2026 and 11 January 2027, so 1 January 2027 entry into force looks out of reach and 1 July 2027 is more likely.
frame_summary: A Dutch payroll publication argues the government's 1 January 2027 target is unrealistic given the parliamentary calendar, though delay does not remove employers' preparation work.
verbatim_quote: De plenaire behandeling staat echter pas gepland op 7 december 2026 en 11 januari 2027.
verbatim_list: treedt de wet waarschijnlijk pas per 1 juli 2027 in werking
